elements.element: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly permits Customer to terminate “this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part.” Nothing limits this right to term-end.

elements.element: Customer’s termination for convenience requires thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires “thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to Vendor.”

elements.element: Upon Customer’s termination for convenience, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires Vendor to “refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination,” which implements a pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The rendered provisions grant Vendor termination rights only for uncured material breach under Section 9.1; they contain no Vendor termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly grants Customer this right.

elements.element: Customer’s termination for convenience requires between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days’ prior notice.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires only thirty (30) days’ prior written notice, not a notice period within the specified 60–90-day fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 states that “no early-termination charge will apply,” so the charge is zero and therefore does not exceed three months’ fees.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, it may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The rendered provisions contain no Vendor termination-for-convenience right, so the condition triggering this restriction is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, Vendor must provide ninety (90) days’ prior notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered provisions contain no Vendor termination-for-convenience right, so the condition triggering the notice requirement is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The redline fully achieves the preferred position: Customer can terminate for convenience on 30 days’ written notice, receives the required refund, incurs no early-termination charge, and Vendor receives no corresponding convenience right. The fallback is not independently satisfied because its specified Customer notice period is 60–90 days, while the clause uses 30 days. The amendment is targeted and leaves the term, breach termination, Order Form separability, and other remedies intact.
